title.narrative: Twuzuzanye (Let's build each other, together): Promouvoir le leadership et la participation politique des femmes à la reconstruction post-conflit, Renforcer la sensibilisation et résilience des jeunes pour lutter contre la manipulation et la militarisation, et Promouvoir des masculinités positives

Twuzuzanye (Let's build each other, together): promoting women’s leadership and political participation in post-conflict reconstruction, building awareness and resilience among youth to counteract manipulation and militarization, and promoting positive masculinities

description.narrative: Burundi has seen cyclical conflicts with disastrous consequences for all. Women and girls have suffered physical violence at the hands of rebels, soldiers, the police, and political actors. Inequality and traditional gender norms in the prevailing patriarchal culture have been exacerbated in a society where militarisation and masculinity are revered. The project is informed by IW’s research expertise and over 10 years of gender work in Burundi. IW’s global ToC recognizes impunity for human rights violations and historical injustices as an impediment to democracy, RoL, and peace. Impunity is the failure to bring perpetrators to justice and deliver redress for victims, but also involves societal factors, political will, and entrenched interests. IW's vision is of a society where human rights are respected, and masculinity is not synonymous with violence. Their strategies build on global WPS and YPS agendas, Burundi’s NAP 1325 and National Development Plan 2018-2027, SDG 5 and 16, and the African Union Transitional Justice Policy. It contributes to Belgian foreign policy priorities on transformative masculinities and women’s empowerment, particularly target 5.5 (women’s full and effective participation in decision-making) and target 10.2 (empowering and promoting inclusion of all by 2030)

Promote positive masculinities and women’s political equality for sustainable peace. SO1: Women’s increased participation in post-conflict reconstruction. SO2: Violent masculinities become less of a risk factor for violence. SO3: Positive masculinities are promoted.

• 48 women leaders. Four women per commune (12/province) will participate in trainings, will initiate community discussion forums, and will lead communal, provincial, and national policy forums. • 4 psychologists who manage provincial psychosocial support centres in the four provinces will provide MHPSS services to the youth ex-combatants, with the support of IW’s partner, THARS. • Women’s rights CSOs. A group of (c.) 10 will be trained to conduct women’s political participation campaigns. • Youth CSOs. A group of (c.) 10 will be trained to conduct community actions on positive masculinities. • 4 youth centres (1/province) trained and supported to implement youth community dialogues on masculinities.
